primary_task: Generate a SHA-256 INTEGRITY.json manifest for an agent plugin directory (and later verify the plugin's files against it) using the Python patterns given.

requirements.name: python3 (stdlib hashlib/json/pathlib)
requirements.evidence:
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path ... manifest = generate_manifest("my-plugin/")
requirements.basis: run shell commands on Linux x86_64: ... build, test, run CLIs and scripts (python3 is standard software of the Linux platform; pip from PyPI is open)

requirements.name: GitHub Actions CI
requirements.evidence: Add to your GitHub Actions workflow: - name: Verify plugin integrity
requirements.basis: The user's GitHub account is usable through the github connector and through the gh CLI via the proxy.

notes: Hashing and manifest generation are pure local Python. The CI integration and promotion gate are optional follow-ups; writing a workflow file is local, while pushing it to GitHub would be an external write (forbid_effects: writes_external) and is not part of the core request. 'Sign this plugin' appears in the trigger list but the document gives no signing procedure, so no signing key is required.
